docs.title: Help
docs.text:
Stems, click, visual cues, video and the score itself, all locked to one transport, on the device in your hand and on every stand. These pages show how to set it up and run it. Each page is one job, a few steps long.

Concert ConductorGet the click in your ear, run a cue from the concert podium, put every stand in sync, show the picture, run a film in concert. Player / Studio ConductorFollow the DAW in the studio or the conductor on stage: set up the device, read your part with the pages turning themselves, practice at home. EngineerInstall the Link plug-ins, lock the podium to Pro Tools or Logic, build cues from your session, publish them.

New to the app? Start with the five-minute quickstart. Something not working? Go straight to If something is wrong.

docs.title: Watch first
docs.text:
Seven short films cover the main setups. Each one also sits at the top of its own page with the written steps underneath.

Concert Conductor Engineer Player / Studio Conductor Connecting audio Building a cue with CueBuilder For musicians Picture on a projector Syncing the podium to a DAW Film in concert Counter for the tracking room

docs.title: Where things are
docs.text:
• Library is the first screen: your cues, folders and programs. The + button imports a cue or starts a program. The toolbar has Audio I/O, Sync, CueBuilder™ and TempoMapper™.
  • Cue view opens when you tap a cue: counter and streamers over the video or the score, transport along the bottom, Click and FOH faders at the sides.
  • Sync Settings (the Sync button) is where a device decides whether it leads, follows, or keeps its own time.
  • The small i buttons throughout the app explain the control next to them. These pages explain the job.

docs.title: If something is wrong
docs.text: The short list, by symptom. Each entry links to the page with the full story.

docs.title: Sound
docs.text:
An output is silent. : Open Audio I/O and check the pair each strip points at. Press Play once, then Copy the log and send it with your report. Audio I/O

The click is late in Bluetooth earbuds. : Move the Earbuds trim in Sync Settings while a cue plays, or calibrate with the microphone. Earbuds on a stand

Sound keeps playing after Stop, or doubles. : Both mixes landing on one pair double. Flip a strip to External and move its pair. Update to 2.9.0 or later, which fixed stray audio after a cue switch on the Mac.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
A stand says waiting to connect. : Same network, and the master must be conducting or have the plug-in inserted on the main output. Guest and corporate Wi-Fi often block device-to-device traffic; a hotspot, a travel router or a USB cable solves it. Conduct the room

The cue starts at the wrong bar when locked to the DAW. : The session, the MIDI file and the stems must share one start timecode and one frame rate. Update the Link plug-ins to version 9 or later. Sync the podium to your DAW

The stand follows, but a fixed amount late. : Give Auto Latency a few locates. Then trim under Manual Latency: late, increase; early, decrease. Sync settings

The stand opens the wrong cue. : Follow Master's Cue switches when the transport stops. Stop, and it switches.

docs.title: Plug-ins
docs.text:
The DAW says Apple could not verify the plug-in. : Install from the app, not by copying. Install the Link plug-ins

Logic shows the plug-in but it never connects. : Insert it on the Stereo Output. Logic idles plug-ins on empty tracks.

Digital Performer does not see it. : Quit and relaunch DP; it examines plug-ins at launch.

docs.title: Picture
docs.text:
External Display Not Available. : The device mirrors only. A separate audience picture needs an M-series iPad or a Mac. Picture on a projector

Picture and orchestra drift apart in the hall. : Adjust House Latency while a cue plays.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text:
A cue shows not in library. : Download it. Programs match cues by title as well as by id.

The next cue did not open. : Choose Refresh Cue Timings in the program's menu after rebuilding a cue. Film in concert

docs.title: Still stuck
docs.text: Write to support through cueconductor.app with the device, the app version from Settings, what you expected, what happened, and the Audio I/O log if sound is involved.

docs.title: Connect the audio
docs.text: The goal: click in your ear, the mix wherever the room needs it, from one device.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• An iPad, iPhone or Mac with CueConductor and a cue.
  • Any of: wired earbuds, a USB audio interface, an HDMI display with sound, or Bluetooth earbuds.

docs.title: Plug in and look
docs.text:
1. Connect the interface or display, then open a cue.
  2. Tap Audio I/O in the Library toolbar, or the speaker button in the cue view.
  3. The sheet shows every output the device is driving right now, as one wide output. HDMI and a USB interface together count every channel each one has.

docs.title: Pick where each thing goes
docs.text:
The Click and FOH strips each have an output pair menu. Tap the pair name on a strip and choose from all available pairs. On a two-output device there is one pair, and both strips share it.

With a stereo pair in your ear, use the pan knobs: push Click hard left and FOH hard right and each ear gets one complete signal. That is the classic podium setup, and CueBuilder can store it as a cue's default routing.

docs.title: Two mixes when the room has its own speakers
docs.text:
A device with more than two outputs, or an interface plus HDMI, can run two complete mixes:

  • Conductor plays on the podium with no delay.
  • External plays to the hall with the house latency from External Display applied.

Flip a Click or FOH strip to External with the switch above the strips to set that mix's fader, mute, pan and pair. The external click starts muted so it never reaches the audience by accident. On a device with only two outputs the switch stays hidden.

docs.title: Bluetooth earbuds
docs.text: With nothing wired attached, the audio goes to Bluetooth earbuds and the click is sent early by the delay iOS reports for them. See Earbuds on a stand for the trim and the microphone calibration.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• An output is silent. Open Audio I/O and tap Copy under the log, then compare the pair each strip points at with the channels the interface shows. Both strips landing on one pair doubles the sound and the pair chip says so.
  • The device changed while playing. Changes made during playback apply at the next Stop.
  • Mac: the sound comes from the wrong device. CueConductor drives its chosen devices directly, independent of the Mac's system output. Choose the device in Audio I/O, not in System Settings.

docs.title: Conduct the room
docs.text: One podium, every stand. Switch on Conduct and every CueConductor on the Wi-Fi follows: counter, beat dots, streamers and page turns, each player reading their own part. No cables, no MIDI, no audio to distribute.

docs.title: On the podium
docs.text:
1. Open the cue.
  2. Tap Sync and switch on Conduct (Broadcast). The sheet reports when it is searching for stands and when they join.
  3. Optionally switch on Push Cues to Stands. Every cue you open is then sent in the background to stands that do not have it: MIDI map, overlay, score and parts and a mono click, no stems or video. A stand that already has the full cue keeps its own.
  4. Press Play. The room follows.

External Sync input is unavailable while conducting; a podium either leads or follows.

docs.title: On each stand
docs.text:
1. Open the same cue, or any cue if the podium pushes cues.
  2. Tap Sync, choose Link to DAW, and leave Follow Master on Any Master.
  3. Switch on Follow Master's Cue so the stand opens whatever cue the podium opens, and Accept Pushed Cues if the podium pushes.

The full player-side steps are on Set up a stand.

docs.title: Several rooms on one network
docs.text: With two podiums or a podium and a DAW on the same Wi-Fi, each stand picks its master under Follow Master. Masters appear in the list once they have tried to connect. Give your device a name under Device Display Name so players can tell rooms apart.

docs.title: USB instead of Wi-Fi
docs.text: A Mac and an iPad connected by cable form a network of their own. Everything above works with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off on both.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• A stand says waiting to connect. Both devices must be on the same network and the podium must have Conduct on. Corporate and guest Wi-Fi often block device-to-device traffic; a hotspot or a travel router solves it.
  • The stand opens the wrong cue. Follow Master's Cue applies when the transport stops, never mid-playback. Stop and it switches.
  • A pushed cue has no sound but click. That is by design. Pushed copies show a Pushed badge in the library and carry no stems or video.

docs.title: Picture on a projector
docs.text: Send the scoring video to a second display or a projector. The audience sees the film; you keep the overlay.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Mac, or an iPad with an M-series chip, for a separate audience picture. Other iPads and iPhones can only mirror their own screen.
  • HDMI or AirPlay to the display.
  • Pro, or a cue licensed for external video.

docs.title: iPad
docs.text:
1. Connect HDMI with the iPad set to mirror. CueConductor takes the display's own full-screen scene: the external picture appears there at full size, and External Display switches on by itself.
  2. Open the cue. The external window shows the film while your screen keeps the overlay.

With Stage Manager extending the display instead, a second window opens; drag it to the external display and use its window controls to go full screen.

docs.title: Mac
docs.text:
1. Open the cue and tap the external display button in the transport.
  2. Tap Open on External Display. A second window opens; drag it to the projector's display and make it full screen.

docs.title: What the audience sees
docs.text:
In the External Display sheet choose the mode:

  • Scoring Video: the package's video only.
  • Video + Overlay: streamers and counter on top.
  • Overlay Only: streamers and counter on black, for when the video comes from another source.

Show Bar Counter hides or shows the counter on the external picture. Fill Screen scales the video to fill the display and crops the edges when the aspect ratio does not match.

docs.title: Keep picture and pit together
docs.text: Projectors and PAs add delay. Set House Latency in milliseconds and the external picture runs ahead by that much, so what the audience sees lands with the orchestra. With Audio uses House Latency on, the External mix follows the same offset. Switch it off for an Audio Latency stepper of its own when sound and picture take different paths, such as HDMI video with the sound on a PA from the interface.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• "External Display Not Available." The device mirrors only. A separate audience picture needs an iPad Pro or iPad Air with an M-series chip, or a Mac. Everything else works.
  • The picture is on the iPad, not the projector. The iPad must be mirroring, not extending with Stage Manager, for the automatic full-screen scene.
  • Picture and sound drift apart. Adjust House Latency while a cue plays; the change applies live.

docs.title: Film in concert
docs.text: A program puts a whole evening's cues on one timeline against the film. The master follows the house clock or is the clock, opens each cue as it arrives, and plays the film on the projector for the whole evening, through the gaps between cues.

docs.title: Build the program
docs.text:
1. Download or build every cue of the evening. Only cues with conductor events can join; that is where each cue's start timecode lives.
  2. In the Library tap + and choose New Program….
  3. Name it. Enter the film start, the timecode of the film's first frame as the house's clock will send it, on the keypad: type the digits and the colons appear. Choose the frame rate.
  4. Tick the cues. They sort themselves by their own start timecodes.
  5. Open the program and choose Add Film Video… to import the full scoring film. Its soundtrack becomes a Film strip in the mixer with the same two mixes as Click and FOH. If the movie carries embedded timecode, the film start is set from it.

Programs sit at the top of the Library. Long-press or right-click one to edit, share, save to disk or delete it.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
The program screen shows the film, the transport, a scrub bar across the whole evening and the list of cues with the next one's countdown.

  1. Open the program. It loads as a local master: Play, Stop and locate here drive the film and every stand, with nothing broadcast yet.
  2. Under Clock choose House clock if QLab or a DAW sends timecode, or This device if the podium is the clock.
  3. Tap Lock. House clock: the device follows the house, opening cues as the time arrives. This device: the device broadcasts as master.
  4. Press Play. Each cue opens a few seconds ahead of its MIDI start so its prep clicks begin exactly on the timecode. The cue runs to its end bar, the program screen returns with the next countdown, and back-to-back cues hand over at the next cue's start.

Locked and rolling, the program screen becomes the stage view between cues: the film fills the screen with the next cue and the countdown over it.

docs.title: Inside a cue during a program
docs.text:
• The cue's video region shows the program film, the same picture the audience sees, with the cue's streamers and counter over it. Overlay Settings has a Picture switch to keep the cue's own video instead.
  • The filmstrip and scrub bar span the whole film, with this cue's stretch marked.
  • Bar and marker locates drive the program transport, and the Program face in the transport toggles Lock and Unlock, so you can navigate as a conductor without leaving the cue.
  • Tap any cue in the list to open it by hand; the clock takes over again when it reaches another.

docs.title: Audio during a program
docs.text: While a cue is open, the film's dialogue and effects run inside that cue's own audio engines beside the click and the FOH mix, so every fader of a mix stays sample-locked for the whole evening. Between cues the program plays the film itself. The hand-over is a short crossfade of identical audio, heard nowhere.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• A cue starts at the wrong bar when locked to Pro Tools. The session, the MIDI file and the stems must share one start timecode, and the frame rate must match. Update the Link plug-ins to version 9 or later; earlier ones mis-reported sessions at 29.97 and 23.976.
  • A cue shows "not in library". Download it; the program finds cues by title as well as by id.
  • The next cue did not open. Cue timings are read from the packages; choose Refresh Cue Timings in the program menu after rebuilding a cue.

docs.title: Run a cue from the podium
docs.text: Everything a conductor touches during a take, and nothing else.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
• Counter: bar, beat dots and meter, over the scoring video.
  • Streamers travel across the picture and land on the beat. A courtesy meter trails the first bar of a new time signature.
  • Transport along the bottom: step back a bar, Play, Stop, step forward a bar, with the time and timecode readout.
  • Click and FOH faders at the sides, each with pan, mute and a meter.
  • Stem mixer: open the drawer to see every stem with its own fader, solo and mute.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• Play starts from the current position after the cue's own pre-roll clicks.
  • Stop parks where you are. Stop twice quickly returns to the start of the cue.
  • Step buttons move one bar at a time while parked.
  • Drag in the scrub bar under the picture to locate anywhere. The filmstrip above it shows where you are in the video.

docs.title: Locate
docs.text:
• Type a bar number and press Go. With playback stopped you land there parked; with playback running you land there playing.
  • The marker list has every rehearsal letter and section name in the cue. Jump & Pause sets a section up; Jump & Play rolls straight into it.

docs.title: Mix without leaving the podium
docs.text: Open the stem drawer. Each stem has a fader, solo and mute. Solo across several stems is a mode, and the master solo button blinks while it is on so you never leave it armed by accident. Restore Defaults returns the mix the cue's author set.

docs.title: Pre-roll
docs.text: The cue's author set how many prep clicks precede the first bar. The counter shows PRE-ROLL and counts them down so you can bring the orchestra in on the downbeat.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• Play does nothing. Check that the device is not locked to a master in Sync Settings; a following device does not start on its own.
  • The picture is black after the last frame. That is the video-less tail of the cue; the counter keeps running to the end bar.
  • The click is late in Bluetooth earbuds. See Earbuds on a stand.

docs.title: Conduct from the score
docs.text: Attach a PDF score and turn the iPad upright. The music replaces the video, with the counter, beat dots and streamers over it, and the pages turn themselves.

docs.title: Get the score into the cue
docs.text: Scores and parts are added in CueBuilder: drop the whole stack of PDFs into Score & Parts and they sort into concert order, name themselves and read their own measure numbers to build the page maps. Cues from the catalog come with theirs.

docs.title: Open it
docs.text:
1. Open the cue and tap Part. Choose Score, or any part.
  2. Turn the iPad to portrait. The page fills the screen.

docs.title: Page turns
docs.text: Pages turn from the cue's own tempo map. Under Page Turns set Turn Early to the number of beats before the page's first bar you want the turn, so your eyes are never on a dead page. A Bluetooth pedal turns pages too.

docs.title: Mark it up
docs.text: Write on the page with Apple Pencil. Markings are kept per part, per device, and travel with the cue when you share it, if you choose to include them.

docs.title: Clear the screen
docs.text:
On iPad the panels around the score collapse:

  • Three dots at the top of the mixer column fold it to a slim tab with Back and the dots.
  • Three dots at the right end of the transport fold it to a slim bar.
  • A tap in the centre of the page brings everything back, at whichever shape you left it.

Each choice is remembered per device. In full screen nothing is drawn over the music.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• Pages turn at the wrong bar. The page map comes from the measure numbers printed on the PDF. Check the first bar of each page in CueBuilder's score preview.
  • The pedal does nothing. Most pedals send page-up and page-down keys; pair it in Settings → Bluetooth and open the score view before testing.

docs.title: Build a cue with CueBuilder
docs.text: Your session becomes a cue. Drop in the MIDI file, stems, score and part PDFs and the scoring video, and CueBuilder turns them into a .conductpkg any CueConductor can play.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A MIDI file exported from the session with the tempo map and meter changes. This is the only required file.
  • Stems as WAV or AIFF, all starting at the same timecode. Include the click as a stem named click.
  • Score and part PDFs, optional.
  • Scoring video, optional, with or without embedded timecode.
  • Pro.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Library tap CueBuilder™.
  2. Sources. Drop each file in its zone, or click a zone to choose. Files dropped anywhere on the sheet are routed by type. Part PDFs sort into concert order and name themselves.
  3. Package. Give it a title. Choose the default routing: Centered puts click and mix in both ears; Split puts the click left and the mix right.
  4. Timecodes. Enter the MIDI file's start timecode on the keypad, digits only. Leave Audio Stems same start time as MIDI File on unless the stems start elsewhere. A video with embedded timecode fills its own start.
  5. Parameters. Frame rate to match the session. Initial meter, streamer duration, and how big a tempo change registers as one.
  6. Meter / Beat Divisions. For each meter change choose the beat grouping, so a 7/8 bar gets streamers on the beats you conduct.
  7. Cue Layout. The bar number the MIDI's first measure displays as, the first bar of prep clicks, the first bar of music and the cue's end bar. Prep clicks and start produce the yellow, white and green events; the end produces the red one.
  8. Annotations. Rehearsal letters and section names as bar=label pairs.
  9. Events. The generated list, live as you change parameters. Delete an auto event to suppress it; Add Manual writes your own streamer or label at any bar and beat.
  10. Preview. Builds a temporary package and plays it through the real engine and overlay. Refresh after edits.
  11. Add to CueConductor installs it in the Library. Compile and Share Package… sends it on; Compile to Folder… writes the file where you choose.

Save the work in progress at any time with Save CueBuilder Project…. Open a saved project or an existing .conductpkg with Open Project or Package… to edit it; the bundled MIDI is reloaded so generation stays live.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• No meter changes appear. The MIDI file has none, or only meters with a single grouping. Export the MIDI from the session with the meter track.
  • The streamers land early or late against the stems. The timecodes differ. Check the MIDI start and the stems' start in the session's clip properties.
  • The library already has this title. Choose Replace to update it, or Rename… to add it beside the old one.

docs.title: Install the Link plug-ins
docs.text: CueConductor Link is a plug-in you insert on your session's main output. It streams the session's transport to the conductor's screen and every stand: sample-accurate, no MIDI setup, no timecode routing. One installer puts all formats in place.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text: DAW Format Pro Tools AAX Logic Pro AU Digital Performer AU (the AU2 component) Cubase, Nuendo, Reaper and others VST3

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Open CueConductor on the Mac.
  2. In the Library tap Tips and choose Install the CueConductor Link DAW plug-ins…. The app also offers this on its second launch if no plug-in is installed.
  3. The macOS Installer opens. Approve it with your password. It places the plug-ins in the system folders and removes any older copies from your user folder.
  4. Quit and relaunch the DAW so it scans for new plug-ins. Digital Performer examines plug-ins at launch; a full quit and reopen is needed.

The app offers the installer again whenever a newer plug-in ships with an update.

docs.title: Insert it
docs.text:
Insert CueConductor Link on the session's main output, the Stereo Output in Logic. Logic idles plug-ins on empty tracks, so an insert elsewhere may not run while the transport is parked.

The plug-in window has a SEND TO list of every CueConductor on the network. A green dot means connected. Tick the devices that should receive the session; by default all of them do.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• The DAW refuses the plug-in with "Apple could not verify…". It was copied by hand or by an old version of the app. Run the installer from the app; its copies are notarized and land without the quarantine mark.
  • Pro Tools does not list it. Only the installer's AAX is PACE-signed. Check /Library/Application Support/Avid/Audio/Plug-Ins/ for CueConductorLink.aaxplugin and rescan.
  • The SEND TO list is empty. The devices must be on the same network as the Mac, or connected by USB cable, with CueConductor open.

docs.title: Counter for the tracking room
docs.text: Put a bar counter, beat dots and streamers in front of the players on the scoring stage, following the session, with no click box per chair.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install the Link plug-in and insert it on the session's main output.
  2. On a device in the room open the cue, tap Sync, choose Link to DAW, and tick Mute Audio During External Sync if the room has its own cue mix. Leave it unticked to feed the click from the device.
  3. Mirror or connect the device to the room's monitor. On a Mac or an M-series iPad, use External Display with Overlay Only for a counter on black.
  4. In the plug-in's SEND TO list tick the device.
  5. Roll the session. The counter follows, through pre-roll and locates, and parks where the session parks.

Several devices can follow at once: one per section, or one on the big screen and one in the booth.

docs.title: Without the cue on the device
docs.text: Switch on Push Cues to Stands in the Mac app's Sync Settings beside the plug-in. The plug-in announces the cue, the Mac app supplies the files, and the device receives a lite copy: MIDI map, overlay, score and parts and a mono click. Stands need Accept Pushed Cues on.

docs.title: Export to QLab
docs.text:
A one-step package for a QLab-driven show: the cue's audio and video with cue numbers, plus the MTC that lets a CueConductor on the podium follow QLab.

  1. Open the cue in CueBuilder, or long-press the cue in the Library.
  2. Choose Export QLab Package… and name the folder.
  3. In QLab, import the package. Each stem arrives as an audio cue, the video as a video cue, all starting together.
  4. On the podium device choose MTC as the sync source and select the MIDI port QLab sends to.

QLab Export needs Pro. The exported package carries the cue's start timecode so the podium lands on bar 1 when QLab's timecode starts there.

docs.title: Share cues, programs and the catalog
Share a cue
docs.text:
Long-press a cue in the Library, or right-click it on the Mac:

  • Share Cue sends the .conductpkg through the share sheet, AirDrop included. If the score carries markings made on this device you are asked whether to include them.
  • Save Cue to Disk… writes the file where you choose.
  • Share Folder… and Share Cues Individually… do the same for a folder.

The receiving device opens the file in CueConductor and it lands in the Library.

docs.title: Share a program
docs.text:
Long-press a program:

  • Share Program Only… sends the program's definition as a .cueprogram: titles, film start, frame rate, the list of cues. Small enough to text.
  • Share with Film… includes the film.
  • Save Program Only to Disk… and Save with Film to Disk… write the files.

A device receiving a program matches its cues by title as well as by id, so cues downloaded separately join it. Cues it does not have show not in library until they are downloaded.

docs.title: Links that open the app
docs.text: Every catalog title has a link of the form https://get.cueconductor.app/<title>. On a device with CueConductor installed the link opens the catalog at that title; without the app it shows the title and a link to the App Store. A PIN travels in the link after #p=, so a texted link downloads straight away.

docs.title: The catalog
docs.text:
Tips → Browse CueConductor Catalog lists every title Vision Music Publishing publishes, in series. Perusal and rehearsal editions are free; performance editions ask for the PIN that came with the licence.

  • PROGRAM entries are whole evenings. Downloading one installs the program; its cues are downloaded separately.
  • COMPANION entries are files that go with a title, such as a Pro Tools session. They download whole and offer Save… to put them where you want.

Titles already in your library say so. Refresh reloads the list.

docs.title: Publishing your own titles
docs.text: The catalog is Vision Music Publishing's. To put your own cues in front of players, share the .conductpkg directly, or host it and send the link; CueConductor opens .conductpkg and .cueprogram files from any source.

docs.title: Sync the podium to your DAW
Sync the podium to your DAW
docs.text: The session is the clock; the conductor's iPad follows it. The position tracks the DAW even while stopped, and the pre-roll counts the conductor in through the session's own pre-roll.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• The Link plug-ins installed on the Mac.
  • The cue on the conductor's device, with Pro or a cue licensed for external sync.
  • The Mac and the device on one network, or a USB cable between them.

docs.title: The one rule
docs.text: The session's start timecode must equal the cue's start timecode, and the frame rates must match. CueBuilder writes the cue's start timecode from the MIDI file; set the session to the same value. A cue whose session, MIDI and stems all start at 01:00:00:00 at 24 fps locks at bar 1.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Insert CueConductor Link on the session's main output.
  2. On the conductor's device open the cue, tap Sync and choose Link to DAW. Under Follow Master, Any Master is fine with one session on the network.
  3. In the plug-in's SEND TO list, make sure the device is ticked. The dot turns green.
  4. Press Play in the DAW. The device chases, and from the next locate on it lands exactly.

Leave Auto Latency on. The device measures its own landing error after every chase and folds it in; the manual offsets become fine trim.

docs.title: Pro Tools on the same Mac
docs.text: CueConductor for Mac reads the plug-in through shared memory, no network at all. Open the cue in the Mac app with Link to DAW chosen and it follows the session on the same machine. iPads on Wi-Fi or USB follow the same session at the same time.

docs.title: Several devices
docs.text: Every CueConductor in the SEND TO list follows the same session: the conductor, the stands, a counter in the tracking room. Untick a device to leave it out. Each device can still pick its master under Follow Master when more than one session is on the network.

docs.title: MTC instead
docs.text: For QLab, show-control rigs and DAWs without the plug-in, choose MTC and select the MIDI port the timecode arrives on. Use the IAC Driver for a DAW on the same Mac, or a network MIDI session for another machine. MTC uses the classic sync engine and manual latency only.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• The cue starts at the wrong bar. The start timecodes differ, or the frame rates do. Fix the session start, or rebuild the cue with the session's start in CueBuilder. Plug-ins before version 9 mis-reported sessions at 29.97 and 23.976; update them from the app.
  • The device never turns green. Same network, CueConductor open with the cue loaded and Link to DAW chosen. Corporate Wi-Fi often blocks it; a USB cable always works.
  • It follows, but late by a fixed amount. Give Auto Latency a few locates. If it stays, add the frames under Manual Latency: late, increase; early, decrease.

docs.title: TempoMapper™
docs.text:
Some cues were played wild: a live take, a rubato performance, a cue composed without a click. TempoMapper™ builds a beat grid against real audio and hands a finished cue to CueBuilder.

  1. In the Library tap TempoMapper™.
  2. Record the audio, import a file, or capture it from the DAW through the Link plug-in. Captured from a DAW, the session's own tempo map arrives as a finished grid.
  3. Play it and tap the tempo as it goes. Anchors land on the taps.
  4. Nudge the anchors onto the transients in the waveform. Set the meter and any meter changes.
  5. Export to CueBuilder. The cue opens with the tempo map in place; add stems, PDFs and video as usual.

TempoMapper™ needs Pro and has its own help inside the editor.

docs.title: Earbuds on a stand
docs.text: With nothing wired attached, an iPad or iPhone sends its audio to Bluetooth earbuds, and the click is sent early by the delay iOS reports for that route, so it lands on the beat. Wired and built-in output are never adjusted.

docs.title: Trim it in
docs.text:
Reported figures are often well short of the truth, especially on Bluetooth speakers.

  1. Connect the earbuds and open a cue.
  2. Tap Sync. The Earbuds row shows the pair's name, the reported figure and how early the click is being sent.
  3. Play the cue and listen against the room or a wired reference. Move Trim until the click sits. It takes effect while playing.

The trim is remembered for that pair of earbuds, so a device tuned once is right every time they reconnect.

docs.title: Calibrate with the microphone
docs.text:
1. In the Earbuds row tap Calibrate with Microphone….
  2. Hold one earbud, or the speaker, to the device's microphone.
  3. Tap Calibrate Earbuds. Five short bursts are played and timed on their way back.
  4. The sheet shows the measured delay against the reported one. Tap Apply to set the trim, or Measure Again.

Calibrate in a quiet moment; the measurement needs to hear the bursts over the room.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• The trim seems to do nothing. It applies live from version 2.9.0 on. On older versions it applied at the next Play.
  • Calibration hears fewer than five bursts. Hold the earbud closer to the microphone and turn the device's volume up.
  • The earbuds are 44.1 kHz and the cue is 48 kHz. iOS resamples; there is no drift.

docs.title: Follow the conductor
docs.text: What the sync controls on a stand do, in the order you meet them.

docs.title: Sync source
docs.text:
• None (Internal Clock): the device keeps its own time. Use it to practice.
  • Link to DAW: follow a conductor's CueConductor or a DAW's Link plug-in. This is the stand setting.
  • MTC: follow MIDI Time Code from QLab or a DAW without the plug-in.

docs.title: Follow Master
docs.text: Any Master accepts whichever podium or plug-in connects, which is fine with one on the network. With two rehearsal rooms on the same Wi-Fi, or a podium and a DAW, pick yours; the others are refused. Masters appear in the list once they have tried to connect.

docs.title: Follow Master's Cue
docs.text: When the master announces which cue is current, open it. A change never interrupts playback; it applies when the transport stops. Off, a banner shows the announced cue and nothing opens by itself.

docs.title: Accept Pushed Cues
docs.text: Receive the cue the master opens, in the background: MIDI map, overlay, score and parts and a mono click. No stems, no video. It arrives under the master's name; a full package you already have is never replaced. Pushed copies show a Pushed badge in the Library.

docs.title: Mute Audio During External Sync
docs.text: Checked, the stand is silent while locked and the master supplies the audio. Unchecked, FOH and click stay live under your own mixer settings while you follow.

docs.title: Auto Latency
docs.text: The stand measures its own landing error after every chase and folds it into sync. A fresh device calibrates itself within a few locates and remembers. The Manual Latency offsets below it become fine trim on top: late by N frames, increase; early, decrease.

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text: Closing the cue disengages sync on this device. The source choice stays for next time.

docs.title: Practice with rehearsal tracks
docs.text:
The same package the conductor uses on stage plays on your own device at home, so nothing on the night is a surprise.

  1. Download the cue from the link or the catalog.
  2. Set the sync source to None (Internal Clock) so the device keeps its own time.
  3. Open the cue and press Play. Click in one ear, the mix in the other, if you pan the faders apart.
  4. Open the stem drawer and turn your own line down, or solo the parts you need to hear.
  5. Jump to any bar by number, or to any rehearsal letter, and loop a passage by locating back to it.

Cues from the catalog marked as perusal or rehearsal editions are free. A cue the conductor pushed to your stand carries only the click and the page, not the stems; download the full cue to practice with the orchestra.

docs.title: Set up a stand
docs.text:
A following device, a player's stand on stage or the conductor's screen in the studio, takes its clock from a master: the concert conductor's device, or the DAW through the Link plug-in. Counter, beat dots, streamers and page turns follow, with your own part on the page. It takes two minutes before the first rehearsal and then looks after itself.

The first-launch question

Choosing Player / Studio Conductor when CueConductor first opens does steps 3 to 6 below for you, with the audio muted while synced. Switch Mute Audio During External Sync off in Sync Settings if you want the click or the mix from this device, for example in earbuds.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• An iPad or iPhone with CueConductor from the App Store. Pro is not needed to follow.
  • The rehearsal Wi-Fi, the same network as the conductor.
  • The cue, from the catalog, from a shared link, or pushed by the conductor.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install the app and open it.
  2. Get the cue. Tap the link the conductor sent, or open Tips → Browse CueConductor Catalog and download it. Enter the PIN if the title asks for one.
  3. Name your device. Tap Sync, scroll to Device Display Name and type something the conductor will recognise, such as "Horn 2".
  4. Follow. In the same sheet choose Link to DAW as the sync source and leave Follow Master on Any Master. Switch on Follow Master's Cue and Accept Pushed Cues.
  5. Pick your part. Open the cue, tap Part and choose yours. Every cue remembers it.
  6. Decide whether this device makes sound. Under Sync Settings, Mute Audio During External Sync keeps it silent while it follows, which is the usual stand. Switch it off for the click and FOH under your own faders, which is what you want with earbuds.

When the conductor presses Play, your screen follows.

docs.title: Earbuds
docs.text: Wired earbuds just work. Bluetooth earbuds work too, and the click is sent early to land on the beat. See Earbuds on a stand for the trim.

docs.title: If it doesn't work
docs.text:
• "Waiting to connect." Same Wi-Fi as the conductor, and the conductor must have Conduct switched on. School and guest networks often block device-to-device traffic; ask for the rehearsal network or a hotspot.
  • The cue does not open when the conductor's does. Follow Master's Cue switches when the transport stops, never mid-playback.
  • The stand shows a different cue than the conductor. Download the cue, or ask the conductor to switch on Push Cues to Stands.

docs.title: Read your part
docs.text:
1. Open the cue and tap Part. The list shows the score and every part the cue carries. Choose yours; the choice follows you across cues.
  2. Turn the device to portrait. The page fills the screen with the counter and beat dots over it.
  3. Pages turn from the conductor's tempo, Turn Early by the number of beats you set, so the next page is up before you need it.

docs.title: Marking the part
docs.text: Write with Apple Pencil, or a finger if you prefer. Markings are kept per part on this device, through updates of the cue.

docs.title: Panels in the way
docs.text: On iPad, the three dots at the top of the side column and at the end of the transport fold those panels away. A tap in the middle of the page brings them back. In full screen nothing is drawn over the music.

docs.title: Several players on one stand
docs.text: Open the score instead of a part, or choose the part that reads best for both. Each stand remembers one part per cue.

docs.title: Audio I/O
docs.text: Everything the device is driving right now, as one wide output.

docs.title: Conductor
docs.text: The device and channel count of the Conductor mix. On iPad and iPhone this is whatever is attached: HDMI and a USB interface together count every channel each one has. On the Mac choose the device here; CueConductor drives it directly, independent of the system output.

docs.title: Output pairs
docs.text: Each Click and FOH strip picks a pair from all available channels. Flip a strip to External with the mix switch to set the External mix's pair. If both mixes land on one pair they double, and the pair chip says so.

docs.title: Mono
docs.text: Fold the External mix to mono, the same signal on both channels of each pair, for a single-speaker or summed PA.

docs.title: The log
docs.text:
What the audio session and the output stage reported: the route and its channel count, the width the output stage was built for, and where each bus landed when the engine started. Copy it and send it when an output is silent. Press Play once before reading it; nothing is logged until the engine starts.

Changes made during playback apply at the next Stop.

docs.title: External Display
docs.text: Opens from the external display button in the cue view's transport.

docs.title: Open on External Display
docs.text: Mac and Stage Manager iPads: a second window opens; drag it to the external display and use its window controls to go full screen. Mirroring iPads: the external picture appears on its own as soon as HDMI is connected, and this switch reflects it.

docs.title: Mode
docs.text:
• Scoring Video: the package's video.
  • Video + Overlay: streamers and counter on top.
  • Overlay Only: streamers and counter on black, when the video comes from another source.

docs.title: Show Bar Counter
docs.text: Hide or show the counter on the external picture. Streamers and beat dots stay. The conductor's own display is unaffected.

docs.title: Fill Screen
docs.text: Scale the video to fill the external window. If the aspect ratios differ the edges are cropped. Off keeps the full frame with letterbox bars.

docs.title: House Latency
docs.text: Projectors and PAs add delay between playback and what the audience sees and hears. The external picture runs ahead by this many milliseconds. Positive values delay the conductor's overlay so the audience stays in sync; negative values compensate for a display that runs ahead. The frame estimate follows the loaded cue's frame rate.

docs.title: Audio uses House Latency
docs.text: On, the External mix runs on the same offset as the picture. Off, an Audio Latency stepper gives the sound its own offset, for when picture and sound take different paths.

docs.title: Audio Output
docs.text: The External mix's device, where the device offers more than one. Flip a Click or FOH strip to External to set its fader, mute, pan and pair. The external click starts muted.

docs.title: Not available
docs.text: An iPad without an M-series chip, and every iPhone, mirrors its own screen and cannot show a separate audience feed. Playback, click, stems and sync work normally.

docs.title: Overlay Settings
docs.text: How the counter and streamers look on this device. Each device keeps its own look.

docs.title: Default
docs.text: On, the overlay draws as it always has and the controls below are ignored. Off, the controls shape it. Custom values are kept either way.

docs.title: Picture
docs.text: What plays behind the overlay on this device while a program runs: the program film, or the cue's own video. The external display always shows the program film.

docs.title: Measure Counter
docs.text: Bar number, beat dots and meter. Size scales the number and the meter label together.

docs.title: Beat Dots and Punches
docs.text: The dots mark the felt beats of the bar; a punch is the flash a landing streamer makes. Each has its own size.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text: The text elements of the overlay. Their size follows the Measure Counter size.

docs.title: Streamers
docs.text: Bar height as a fraction of the overlay, and position up or down. Two switches add streamers the cue's author did not write: one at every barline, one at every beat, each travelling a constant three seconds.

docs.title: Direction
docs.text: Streamers travel left to right, right to left, or drop from the top. The courtesy meter trails on the approach side.

docs.title: Sync settings
docs.text: The Sync button opens this sheet in the Library and in the cue view. One sheet decides whether the device leads, follows, or keeps its own time.

docs.title: Sync source
docs.text: Choice What it does None (Internal Clock) The device keeps its own time. Link to DAW Follows a DAW session through the Link plug-in, or a conducting CueConductor. Sample-accurate, no MIDI setup; the position tracks the master even while stopped. The session's start timecode should match the cue's. MTC MIDI Time Code from the selected port. Use the IAC Driver for a DAW on the same Mac, or a network MIDI session for another machine. Covers QLab and show-control rigs.

docs.title: Follow Master
docs.text: Which master this device listens to. Any Master accepts whichever podium or plug-in connects. With more than one on the network, pick yours; the others are refused. Masters appear once they have tried to connect.

docs.title: Follow Master's Cue
docs.text: Open the cue the master announces. Applies when the transport stops, never mid-playback. Off, a banner shows the announced cue.

docs.title: Accept Pushed Cues
docs.text: Receive the master's cue in the background as a lite copy: MIDI map, overlay, score and parts, mono click. A full package you already have is never replaced. Pushed copies carry a Pushed badge.

docs.title: Mute Audio During External Sync
docs.text: Checked, the device is silent while locked and the master supplies the audio. Unchecked, FOH and click stay live under your own mixer settings.

docs.title: Auto Latency (learned)
docs.text: Measures this device's landing error after every Link chase and folds it into sync. A fresh device calibrates itself within a few locates and remembers. Applies to Link and conductor sync; MTC stays manual.

docs.title: Manual Latency
docs.text: Hand trim on top of Auto Latency, or alone when Auto is off. Start governs entries from the top of the cue; Mid-Cue governs locates past the beginning. Leave Same as Start on unless they need different values. Late by N frames, increase; early, decrease.

docs.title: Conductor Mode
docs.text:
• Conduct (Broadcast): stream this device's playback to every stand on the network. No audio. External sync input is unavailable while conducting.
  • Push Cues to Stands: send a lite copy of each cue you open to stands that lack it. Also works on a Mac beside a Link plug-in: the plug-in announces the cue, the app supplies the files.
  • Device Display Name: how this device appears in the plug-in's SEND TO list and to other devices.

docs.title: Earbuds
docs.text: Shown when Bluetooth carries the audio: the pair's name, the reported delay, the trim, and Calibrate with Microphone…. See Earbuds on a stand.

docs.title: Classic Sync Engine
docs.text: Fallback to the previous engine. The current one drives the overlay straight from the master clock and starts audio and video on hardware-scheduled appointments. Flip this only if the new engine misbehaves, and re-engage sync afterwards. MTC always uses the classic engine.

docs.title: Words we use
docs.text:
Cue : One piece of music as a package: MIDI tempo map, stems, click, scoring video, score and parts, and the conductor events that draw the streamers. Files end in .conductpkg.

Program : An evening's cues on one timeline against a single film. The program opens each cue as the clock reaches it. See Film in concert.

Stand : Any device that follows a master: a player's iPad or iPhone, the podium following a DAW, a counter in the tracking room.

Master : The device or session that owns the clock. A podium with Conduct (Broadcast) on, a DAW with the Link plug-in, or a program running on This device.

Link : CueConductor's own sync. The Link plug-in in a DAW, or a conducting device, streams the transport to every stand over Wi-Fi or a USB cable. Sample-accurate, no MIDI.

MTC : MIDI Time Code. The older way to follow QLab, show-control rigs or a DAW without the Link plug-in.

Streamer : The bar that travels across the picture and lands on a beat. Yellow and white for prep clicks, green for the start of music, red for the end, plus whatever the cue's author wrote.

Punch : The flash a landing streamer makes.

Click : The metronome track in the cue, on its own fader and output pair.

FOH mix : Front of house. The stems summed on one fader, with its own output pair, for the hall or the conductor's other ear.

Conductor and External mixes : Two complete mixes. Conductor plays on the podium with no delay. External plays to the hall or projector with the house latency applied, so picture and sound reach the audience together.

House latency : The delay a projector or PA adds. Set once in External Display; the external picture and mix run early by that much.

Lite cue / pushed cue : The copy a master sends to stands that do not have the cue: MIDI map, overlay, score and parts, mono click. No stems, no video.

Catalog : The list of cues and programs from Vision Music Publishing inside the app, some free, some unlocked with a PIN.

CueBuilder™ : The tool inside the app that turns MIDI, stems, PDFs and video into a cue.

TempoMapper™ : The tool that builds a tempo map against real audio for music recorded without a click.

docs.title: Free and Pro
docs.text:
Everyone can browse the catalog, import cues, play them with click and mix, follow a conductor on a stand and share cues. That covers every player and most rehearsals.

Pro unlocks the tools that create and lead:

  • Build .conductpkg in CueBuilder, and export events.
  • External Sync: following a DAW over Link or MTC.
  • External Video on a projector or second display.
  • QLab Export.
  • TempoMapper™.

Pro comes with a free trial. A cue bought with a licence may include external sync for that cue; the Library marks those Licensed. Devices that downloaded the app during the launch promotion have Pro for life.

Tapping a Pro control while locked shows what it unlocks and takes you to the store. Nothing you have already set up is lost.

docs.title: Five-minute quickstart
docs.text: By the end of this page you will have heard a cue with its click, seen the counter and streamers, and connected a second device as a stand.

docs.title: 1. Get a cue
docs.text:
1. Open CueConductor. The Library is empty the first time.
  2. Tap Tips in the toolbar and choose Browse CueConductor Catalog.
  3. Pick a title marked as a perusal edition and tap Download. Titles with a PIN need the code that came with your licence.
  4. The cue appears in the Library when the download finishes.

docs.title: 2. Play it
docs.text:
1. Tap the cue. The cue view opens with the first bar on the counter.
  2. Press Play. You hear the click and the mix, and the streamers fly across the picture ahead of each landing.
  3. Press Stop. Press it again quickly to go back to the start.
  4. Drag the Click and FOH faders at the sides. The pan knobs fold each to one ear when you push them hard to a side.

docs.title: 3. Jump around
docs.text:
• Type a bar number in the locate strip and press Go to jump there, with or without playback.
  • Tap a rehearsal letter in the marker list. Jump & Pause sets up a section; Jump & Play rolls straight into it.

docs.title: 4. Connect a stand
docs.text:
On a second iPad or iPhone on the same Wi-Fi:

  1. Install CueConductor and download the same cue.
  2. Open the cue, tap Sync, and choose Link to DAW. Leave Follow Master on Any Master.

Back on your own device:

  1. Tap Sync and switch on Conduct (Broadcast).
  2. Press Play. The stand's counter, beat dots and streamers follow you. It hears no audio from you; it only follows.

Which device is the conductor?

Any device can lead. Whichever one has Conduct (Broadcast) switched on is the master for that cue. Switch it off to make the device an ordinary stand again.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
• Connect the audio for a USB interface, HDMI or earbuds.
  • Set up a stand for what players need to know.
  • Sync the podium to your DAW if a session is the clock.
